chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May Allah have mercy on you! What is the beautiful patience?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is a patience wherein is no complaining to the people.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of beautiful patience in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'beautiful patience' (al-sabr al-jamil) is characterized by refraining from complaining to other people, a definition that aligns with the Prophet’s example in Surah Yusuf. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining dignity and avoiding burdening others with one's trials, while still allowing for private supplication to God. The narration serves as a practical guide for emotional regulation within the community, ensuring that patience is both spiritually sincere and socially considerate.
